exposure: Mode of delivery (planned vaginal birth vs cesarean birth)
cohort: 33,812 women in British Columbia with singleton term births (37-41 weeks of gestation) and 1-2 prior cesarean births, excluding those with gestational hypertension, pre-existing diabetes, and cardiac disease
finding: After 1 or 2 previous cesarean births, risks for adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes associated with planned vaginal birth compared to cesarean birth are reduced among women with a prior vaginal birth.
mod_finding: Planned vaginal birth was associated with an elevated risk for life-threatening maternal outcomes but a decreased risk of non-life threatening maternal and neonatal outcomes in women with a prior vaginal birth, compared to planned cesarean birth.
